findings.summary: the first fix gave GpuBufferUploadBatch an explicit release() the scene loop had to remember to call before release(state) -- a call-to-remember, and a public released-but-alive state nothing needs; every sibling SDL run loop instead tears down after its try, so the scene loop now does the same and try-scoped run-lifetime objects (the batch, the pick hook guard) unwind before the device by construction; the method, its call, its comment and the pin that spelled it are gone, and the header is byte-identical to main

~ContextRecord's device.reset() was inert -- in the pinned LabSound the destination node and the device co-own each other, so ~AudioDeviceSdl3 never runs from a record -- and its comment described that never-running destructor as the join; the body is now the one effective line, device->stop(), and the comment states the operating mechanism (a returned SDL pause is a join under the device lock, and member order would free the graph first)

the record destructor orders the record's own members but cannot order the record against the rest of the program: contexts() is a function-local static, generated code closes a context only on disposeAudioEngine, so every demo's audio threads ran into static destruction on both backends; run_engine's exit guard -- the one place a run ends, already named as such by pal_audio.hpp -- now closes every context after the captures rendered (AudioCaptureOnExit became AudioRunEnd)

the two SDL_WasInit guards in AudioDeviceSdl3 repeated the same predicate, the same stream_ pre-check and the same comment; one stream_alive() carries the rationale once and both the destructor and stop() ask it

the three text pins spelled statements (an exact if-body, the destructor's two lines including the inert reset, the explicit release call), so a behaviour-preserving refactor would fail them while the invariant held; two pins now guard the structures that carry the invariants -- the scene loop's release(state) sits after its catch, and run_engine's exit guard closes the contexts after rendering captures -- and the batch pin's whole-file read shares the sibling test's idiom

audio_close_context pauses the device explicitly and then erasing the record pauses it again through the new destructor; the explicit pause precedes the destination disconnect on purpose and the second is a no-op on a paused device, so both stay
findings.blockedBy: not blocked: the ordering is intentional (pause before disconnect) and the duplicate pause is a no-op; removing the explicit call would reorder a deliberate sequence for no gain
findings.filedIn: none -- resolved as intended behaviour, nothing to file
